claims.claim_text: Exact private-identifier agreement confirms the indexed Carl A. Bova identity in the official Army merged file.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The index and Army record share the exact private identifier, full name, and middle initial; Naugatuck newspaper notices independently corroborate his draft and induction context.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed through exact private-identifier agreement across official sources, with independent contemporary name, place, and induction corroboration.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Army record dates entry to November 17, 1942. It does not establish the later Army-to-OSS assignment date.
claims.match_notes: The full identifier remains masked publicly. The index's corporal grade may reflect later promotion and does not conflict with private-at-entry grade.

claims.claim_text: The official Army entry record places Carl A. Bova in the broad civilian group for semiskilled paper-goods manufacturing occupations.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Code 642 was recorded at Army entry on November 17, 1942 and maps to semiskilled occupations in manufacture of paper goods.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed exact private-identifier match with contemporary induction corroboration.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded at Army entry; not a named employer and not proven to be the immediate predecessor to OSS.
claims.match_notes: No paper company, workplace, exact trade, or Army-to-OSS sequence is inferred.

claims.claim_text: The private identifier printed for Gordon L. Bovee resolves to a differently named person in the official Army merged file; the conflict is retained and neither identity is promoted.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Identifier resolves to a different name.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The visually checked index identifier produced one official Army record, but its name does not match Gordon L. Bovee.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Conflicting. An identifier alone cannot override a wholly different name when the official file itself warns of duplicate and corrupted values.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Army record cannot be assigned to the indexed person, so its chronology and occupation are withheld.
claims.match_notes: The full identifier and the unrelated Army-record name remain private.

claims.claim_text: A scholarly study's item-level citations to August 1945 OSS China correspondence support a high-confidence match for the index's rare Robert G. Bowdler name.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The study cites three Clyde Sargent messages to Robert G. Bowdler in an OSS Kunming file between August 1 and 10, 1945.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence. The rare exact full name appears both in the official personnel index and item-level citations to OSS China correspondence, but the underlying letters were not reviewed.
claims.temporal_assessment: The correspondence explicitly dates OSS activity to August 1945; it does not document Robert G. Bowdler's pre-OSS employer or earlier military assignment.
claims.match_notes: A 1935 university-yearbook namesake and other biographical candidates are not linked to this entity. Box 72 or the cited Kunming correspondence is required before adding biographical details.

claims.claim_text: Exact private-identifier agreement confirms Harold L. Bowen's Army record, but its November 1, 1945 entry date postdates OSS and cannot support a pre-OSS occupation claim.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The index and Army record share the exact private identifier and name. NARA states that OSS ended by presidential order in September 1945, effective October 1.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed through exact private-identifier and full-name agreement across official sources.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Army record begins after OSS ceased to exist. Its civilian-occupation code is deliberately excluded from pre-OSS findings, and the sequence requires personnel-file review.
claims.match_notes: The full identifier remains masked. No assumption is made about whether the record reflects reenlistment, transfer, data error, or post-OSS service.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The index supplies Michel Bouvier without rank or a usable private identifier. Exact-name and variant official, OSS, CIA Reading Room, employer, occupation, obituary, directory, newspaper, institutional, and archival searches produced no candidate meeting the identity threshold.
person_updates.next_action: No reliable pre-OSS employer has yet been identified in the accessible sources reviewed. Review Box 72 for identity and employment chronology.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The visually verified index identifier resolves in the official Army file to a wholly different name. Because the file documentation warns of duplicate and corrupted values, neither the Army identity nor its occupation is assigned to Gordon L. Bovee.
